prediction.named_residual: discretization-induced jump sensitivity in cycle_residual measurement, previously documented in noise_robustness_v1 (PR #2) and mix_axis_smoothness_v1 (PR #9). Predict that a finer-binned fingerprint (20 bins instead of 6) reduces the mix-axis max/median jump ratio below 5.0, which would resolve the discretization weakness on that axis.

kill_condition.rule: fail if max(|diff|)/median(|diff|) > 5.0 across 21-sample mix sweep when using the 20-bin fingerprint. Equivalent to the kill condition of mix_axis_smoothness_v1 (PR #9) applied to the alternative fingerprint. A PASS demonstrates that binning resolution alone resolves the discretization weakness; a FAIL indicates the issue is deeper than binning.
kill_condition.rationale: The kill condition is identical in form to mix_axis_smoothness_v1's, so a direct PASS/FAIL comparison answers whether finer binning is a real fix. The threshold (5.0) is the same as the prior voice; only the fingerprint resolution differs.

verdict.rationale: Fine-fingerprint (20-bin) max/median jump ratio = 5.78, exceeds threshold 5.0. Baseline was 2813.9; improvement factor 486.8× is insufficient. The discretization issue is deeper than binning resolution — likely the categorical max-utilization element or the histogram-projection itself. Voice enters null-voice ledger per §3.4.
